name: InSight

site.name: Elysium Planitia (Homestead Hollow)
site.description: Flat equatorial volcanic plain selected for stable seismic ground coupling and year-round solar illumination.

endCause: Progressive Martian dust accumulation on the twin circular solar arrays lowered power output until battery reserves depleted after 1,440 sols.
scientificValue: InSight deployed the first ultra-sensitive broadband seismometer directly onto the Martian regolith using a robotic arm. By tracking seismic waves generated by marsquakes and meteoroid impacts, the lander mapped Mars' crustal thickness, mantle structure, and liquid metallic core.

legacy.finding: Cataloged 1,319 marsquakes over four Earth years via the SEIS instrument, including a magnitude-5 event recorded on May 4, 2022.
Used core-reflected seismic waves to determine that Mars possesses a liquid core with a radius of roughly 1,800 to 1,830 kilometers.
Measured surface pressure drops, magnetic anomalies, and seismic-acoustic signatures of fresh meteoroid crater impacts.

image.alt: Monochrome technical schematic of the NASA InSight lander showing its twin circular solar arrays, deployment arm, and surface-deployed SEIS seismometer dome.
